settings.thinkingNotConfigurable: This model's template does not read a thinking toggle — reasoning depth is set by Reasoning effort below.
settings.effortHelpMistral: Mistral 4: Auto = fast (no reasoning), High = deep step-by-step reasoning.
settings.effortHelpGeneric: Controls thinking depth for models that support it. Default uses the model's own setting.
settings.temperatureHelp: Controls randomness. Lower = more focused, higher = more creative.
settings.mtpTempDefault: Native MTP Auto uses greedy startup defaults (temperature 0). This is not a forced limit: explicit API/chat sampling settings can override these defaults.
settings.mtpTempPinned: Temperature is 0 because Native MTP is in Deterministic mode, which enforces greedy decoding. Select Auto in Server Settings to allow explicit request sampling overrides.
settings.mtpTempActive: Native MTP Auto is preserving temperature {{temperature}} and using stochastic speculative verification.
settings.mtpTempInactive: Native MTP is in Deterministic mode, but the displayed temperature is {{temperature}}. Reopen Chat Settings or select Auto before sampling.
settings.topPHelp: Nucleus sampling. Keeps the smallest set of highest-probability tokens whose cumulative probability reaches this threshold.
settings.maxTokensHelp: Maximum new tokens for responses in this chat. Leave blank to use the bundle's generation_config/jang_config value when declared, otherwise the engine fallback; set a value here or send max_tokens/max_output_tokens in the API request to override it.
settings.maxThinkingTokensHelp: Leave blank to preserve the model/runtime native default and the request's full output budget. Only an explicit value in this UI or API max_thinking_tokens sets a separate reasoning cap. Models without thinking-budget support may ignore it.
settings.topKHelp: Limits tokens to top K candidates. 0 = disabled (uses Top P only).
settings.minPHelp: Minimum probability threshold relative to top token. 0 = disabled.
settings.repetitionPenaltyHelp: Penalizes repeated tokens. 1.0 = no penalty. Leave Server default to use the model bundle defaults instead of applying a global penalty.
settings.frequencyPenaltyHelp: OpenAI-compatible count-based token penalty from -2 to 2. Positive values increasingly penalize tokens each time they repeat; 0 is neutral.
settings.presencePenaltyHelp: OpenAI-compatible one-time token-presence penalty from -2 to 2. Positive values encourage new tokens; 0 is neutral.

config.powerManagementDesc: Control when idle models automatically sleep to free GPU memory. Sleeping models auto-wake when a new request arrives.
config.autoSleepDesc: Automatically put the model to sleep after a period of inactivity to free memory. Light sleep clears caches but keeps the model loaded (instant wake). Deep sleep unloads the model entirely (2-15s wake). Models auto-wake when a new request arrives.
config.putSleepOnIdle: Put model to sleep when idle (frees GPU memory)
config.imageEditServerNote: This is an image editing server. Only server settings (host, port, timeout) apply. Use the Image tab to edit images or call /v1/images/edits.
config.imageGenServerNote: This is an image generation server. Only server settings (host, port, timeout) apply. Use the Image tab to generate images or call /v1/images/generations.
config.onlyCompressesSavedPrefixes: This only safely compresses saved prefixes
config.coreEngineHandlesVision: The core engine handles Vision models automatically.
config.prefixCachingWorksForImages: Prefix caching works for images too!
config.sleepWhenIdle: Put model to sleep when idle (frees GPU memory)
config.fuseMetalOps: Fuse Metal operations for faster inference (experimental)
config.hostTooltip: The network interface to bind to. Default 127.0.0.1 (localhost only). Change to 0.0.0.0 to allow connections from other machines on your network (LAN access). Use an API key when binding to 0.0.0.0.
config.portTooltip: The TCP port the server listens on. Each running model instance needs a unique port. Ports are auto-assigned starting from 8000. You can manually set any port between 1024-65535 that isn't already in use.
config.apiKeyTooltip: Optional authentication key for the OpenAI-compatible API. When set, all API requests must include this key in the Authorization header. Leave empty to allow unauthenticated access (fine for local-only servers).
config.servedModelNameTooltip: Custom name to expose via the /v1/models API and in response objects. When set, API clients can use this name instead of the full model path. Both the custom name and the actual model name are listed in /v1/models. Leave empty to auto-derive from model path (e.g. 'mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B').
config.rateLimitTooltip: Maximum number of API requests allowed per minute. Set to 0 to disable rate limiting. Useful when exposing the server to multiple users or external applications to prevent overloading.
config.timeoutTooltip: Maximum time in seconds to wait for a single inference request to complete before timing out. Increase this for very long generations or slow models. Default is 300s for most models; MiniMax-M3 and DSV4 auto-use 900s unless you choose a custom value.
config.logLevelTooltip: Controls how much detail the server logs. DEBUG shows everything (very verbose). INFO is the default. WARNING and ERROR reduce noise to only important messages.
config.corsOriginsTooltip: Allowed origins for cross-origin API requests (from web browsers). Use * to allow all origins, or a comma-separated list of specific origins (e.g. http://localhost:3000,https://myapp.com). Only matters when external web apps call your API.
config.concurrentHint: Controls how many requests your server handles at once. Keep Continuous Batching ON to enable the caching engine.
config.maxConcurrentSequencesTooltip: Maximum number of sequences (requests) that can be processed simultaneously. Higher values allow more parallel users but consume more memory. For single-user local use, 1-4 is sufficient. For multi-user servers, 16-256 depending on available RAM.
config.prefillBatchSizeTooltip: Maximum number of concurrent prompts processed in parallel during the prefill (prompt processing) phase. Higher = more parallelism for multi-user workloads, more memory pressure during prompt ingest.
config.prefillStepSizeTooltip: Maximum number of tokens processed in a single prefill forward pass per sequence. Larger = fewer kernel launches and faster prefill, more transient memory. Reduce if you OOM mid-prompt on long contexts.
config.completionBatchSizeTooltip: Maximum number of tokens to generate in a single completion (token generation) step. Similar to prefill batch size but for the generation phase. Larger values can improve throughput for multi-user scenarios.
config.smeltModeTooltip: Partial expert loading for MoE models. Loads backbone + N% of experts from SSD, reducing RAM by ~50% while maintaining ~97% baseline speed via cache-biased routing and native SwitchGLU kernels.
config.smeltDisabledDsv4: Smelt is disabled for DSV4 Flash. DSV4 uses the verified native JANG affine loader and composite cache path.
config.smeltDisabledFlashMoe: Smelt is disabled while Flash MoE is on. They both modify MoE expert layers — use one or the other.
config.smeltExpertsHint: Loading {percent}% of experts per MoE layer. Lower = less RAM, slightly more routing bias.
config.flashMoeTooltip: Streams MoE expert weights from SSD on-demand instead of keeping them all in RAM. Enables massive MoE models (35B-397B) to run on machines with limited RAM by caching only recently-used experts in a slot-bank cache. Incompatible with Smelt, Distributed, and JIT. ~50% slower than full-RAM mode due to on-demand disk loading.
config.flashMoeDisabledDsv4: Flash MoE is disabled for DSV4 Flash. DSV4 native expert hydration and SWA+CSA/HCA cache restore are not compatible with SSD expert streaming.
config.flashMoeDisabledSmelt: Flash MoE is disabled while Smelt is on. Turn it off to enable Flash MoE.
config.flashMoeDisabledDistributed: Flash MoE is disabled while Distributed is on. Turn it off to enable Flash MoE.
config.slotBankSizeTooltip: Number of expert weight sets cached in RAM. Higher = more cache hits but more RAM. Recommended: 64 for Nemotron/small MoE, 256+ for Qwen3.5 MoE, 512+ for MiniMax (256 experts).
config.ioWorkersTooltip: Number of parallel disk I/O threads for loading experts. Higher = faster cold loads but more I/O pressure. Default 4 works well for most SSDs.
config.flashMoeStreamingHint: Streaming experts from SSD with {slots}-slot LRU cache. Non-MoE models automatically pass through (no effect). JIT disabled (incompatible with on-demand loading).
config.continuousBatchingTooltipDsv4: DSV4 Flash requires the continuous-batching DSV4BatchGenerator path. Prefix reuse uses its native SWA+CSA/HCA typed cache; the RAM paged tier and persistent Block Disk L2 remain independently configurable.
config.continuousBatchingTooltip: Keep ON for best performance. This is the master switch for Prefix Cache, In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM), Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2), and stored-cache codecs. Turning it off uses the direct single-request engine and disables the cache features below.
config.continuousBatchingHint: Keep ON for best overall behavior: it enables prefix reuse, the in-memory RAM tier, persistent SSD L2, and architecture-specific cache restore while the default max sequence count stays at one for local chat.
config.dsv4BatchPathNote: DSV4 Flash stays on its native DSV4BatchGenerator path. Prefix reuse defaults On and Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) defaults On as the warm/cold stack. In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) remains optional and bounded when enabled; the CSA/HCA pool codec remains bundle-derived.
config.cacheFlagsOmittedNote: Cache flags will be omitted at launch while continuous batching is off. Turn it back on to use Prefix Cache, In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM), Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2), and stored-cache codecs.
config.batchingOffDisablesNote: Turning this off disables Prefix Cache, In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM), KV cache quantization, and disk caching. Enable it to unlock these features.
config.prefixCacheHint: Speeds up repeated conversations by remembering previous prompts. Makes follow-up messages much faster (lower time-to-first-token).
config.dsv4PrefixReuseNote: DSV4 prefix reuse preserves the native SWA plus CSA/HCA composite state. It is controlled by this standard Prefix Cache switch; there is no separate hidden DSV4 cache toggle.
config.openPanguTypedCacheNote: openPangu v2 uses exact typed N-1 prompt snapshots. Memory and prompt-disk L2 preserve MLA KV, DSA indexer state, rotating-SWA metadata, and all three causal-convolution states together. Generic paged blocks, reverse truncation, and generic KV q4/q8 stay off.
config.prefixCacheRequiresBatching: Prefix cache requires continuous batching. Turn on 'Continuous Batching' in the Concurrent Processing section above to enable prefix caching.
config.enablePrefixCacheTooltip: Caches prompt prefixes so repeated system prompts, documents, and conversation history can reuse their computed state instead of repeating prefill. The selected RAM and/or SSD tier below owns where reusable blocks are retained. Reused state is not recomputed, so a cached turn can word an answer slightly differently than an uncached one; turn this off if you need byte-identical replay.
config.openPanguMemoryAwareNote: Memory-aware mode is required for openPangu's non-aliasing typed cache clone. The legacy entry-count backend is unavailable for this family.
config.legacyEntryCountCacheTooltip: Switches from memory-aware cache (which uses Cache Memory %, Cache Memory Limit, and Cache TTL controls) to a simpler entry-count cache. When ON: you control cache by max entries only. When OFF: you get fine-grained memory budget controls (% of RAM, MB limit, TTL expiration). Memory-aware mode is recommended for most users.
config.legacyModeActiveNote: Legacy mode active — Cache Memory %, Cache Memory Limit, and Cache TTL are hidden. Turn off 'Legacy Entry-Count Cache' above to use memory-aware caching with those controls.
config.maxCacheEntriesTooltip: Maximum number of prefix cache entries to store when using legacy entry-count mode. Each entry stores the KV cache for one unique prefix. Higher values cache more prefixes but use more memory. For finer control over memory usage, switch to memory-aware mode by unchecking 'Legacy Entry-Count Cache' above.
config.prefixCacheMaxBytesTooltip: Optional global byte budget for the legacy entry-count prefix cache. When set, eviction also fires when total cached bytes exceed this. Eviction priority is assistant → user → system, so shared system prompts persist across users/sessions. 0 = unlimited (entry-count only).
config.cacheMemoryLimitTooltip: Hard limit on memory used by the prefix cache in megabytes. Set to 'Auto-detect' to let the system auto-detect based on available RAM and the percentage setting below. Set an explicit value if you need to reserve memory for other applications.
config.cacheMemoryPercentTooltip: Percentage of available system RAM to allocate for the prefix cache. Only used when Cache Memory Limit is set to 'Auto-detect'. Default 15% leaves headroom for model weights and active generation. Higher values cache more prefixes but risk memory pressure during long generations.
config.blockDiskOnlyBudgetNote: In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) is Off and Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) is authoritative, so Cache Memory Limit, Cache Memory %, and Cache TTL do not apply. Block Size and Max Cache Blocks bound the in-memory hash/index capacity; Block Cache Max bounds SSD usage.
config.cacheTtlTooltip: Time-to-live for memory-aware cache entries. Entries not accessed within this window are evicted to free memory. 'No expiration' means entries are only evicted by memory pressure. This setting has no effect while In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) is on; that tier uses LRU eviction based on Max Cache Blocks.
config.cachingHelpBatchBody: is the heart of vMLX's server performance. Unlike simple mode (which processes exactly one request at a time), continuous batching allows multiple requests to be processed simultaneously. More importantly, it is required to enable all advanced caching features (Prefix Cache, In-Memory Paged Cache, KV Quantization, and Disk Cache).
config.cachingHelpPrefixBody: Prefix caching drastically speeds up interactions by remembering previous prompts (like a system prompt or a long document), skipping the expensive prefill phase.
config.memoryAwareDefaultBody: Intelligently manages the cache based on explicit memory boundaries (MB) or a percentage of total system RAM. It automatically evicts the oldest items when crossing these limits.
config.legacyEntryCountBody: A simpler system that just stores a fixed number of complete prompt states regardless of their size. Useful if you want strict deterministic eviction.
config.cachingHelpMambaBody: Newer models like Qwen 2.5/3, Falcon Mamba, and Jamba mix standard Attention (KV cache) with SSM blocks (Mamba/Arrays cache).
config.kvQuantizationBody: vMLX securely isolates Mamba layers. If you turn on KV Quantization (e.g. q8), it will safely compress the Attention layers while leaving the internal Mamba/SSM memory at full precision, ensuring no corruption or quality loss.
config.inMemoryPagedCacheBody: Some models use this RAM tier when Prefix Cache is enabled so attention KV blocks and path-dependent state share one cache contract. Supported models can instead use Block Disk Cache as an SSD-only tier.
config.kvQuantHelpBody1: By converting stored prompts to q8 or q4 precision, you can reduce the cache's RAM footprint by 2-4x.
config.kvQuantHelpBody2: The actual text generation continues to run at standard full precision natively in MLX.
config.vlHelpBody: If you repeatedly ask questions about the exact same image (like in a tool-calling flow analyzing a dashboard), the massive vision embedding prefill is cached and reused instantly.
config.pagedCacheHint: Locked off for this release. vMLX persists reusable prefix and native cache blocks to SSD and restores payloads only transiently; it does not launch a retained paged-RAM mirror.
config.dsv4PagedNote: DSV4 uses fixed 256-token typed composite blocks in the authoritative SSD tier. Its retained paged-RAM mirror is disabled.
config.pagedCacheRequiresBatching: In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) requires continuous batching. Turn on 'Continuous Batching' in the Concurrent Processing section above to enable the RAM cache tier.
config.pagedCacheDiskConflict: In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) and legacy Disk Cache cannot run simultaneously. Enabling the RAM tier will auto-disable legacy Disk Cache. For persistent SSD caching, use 'Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2)' below instead.
config.pagedCacheEnablesPrefix: In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) is a prefix-cache backend. Turning it on will enable Prefix Cache.
config.nativePagedRequiresPrefix: This model uses a native/in-memory paged cache when Prefix Cache is enabled. Enable Prefix Cache above to activate the architecture-specific cache stack.
config.zayaTypedCacheNote: ZAYA CCA SSD prefix reconstruction is not yet available. Paged RAM remains locked off, so ZAYA clean-prefills instead of reporting a false cache hit.
config.nativeCacheRequiresPagedNote: This model's retained paged-RAM route is disabled. Only source-proven SSD reconstruction may claim prefix reuse.
config.dsv4SsdOnlyNote: DSV4 SSD-only mode preserves typed SWA plus CSA/HCA state in Block Disk L2 without claiming a retained RAM payload tier.
config.dsv4RamL1Note: DSV4's retained RAM tier is disabled; its bundle-derived typed records use the authoritative SSD tier.
config.stepSsdOnlyNote: Step full/sliding-KV SSD-only mode is available: typed KV blocks and rotating metadata stay in Block Disk L2 without RAM payloads. Under tight Metal headroom, long cold-prompt stores can be skipped to avoid an unsafe second clean prefill; existing SSD blocks remain reusable.
config.mixedSwaSsdOnlyNote: Native sliding/mixed-SWA SSD-only mode keeps typed KV blocks and rotating-window metadata in Block Disk L2 without retaining RAM payloads.
config.hybridSsdOnlyNote: Hybrid/Mamba SSD-only mode keeps attention KV blocks in Block Disk L2 while restoring full-precision SSM/GDN companion state from its typed SSD store or clean-prefill rederive.
config.m3SsdOnlyNote: MiniMax-M3 SSD-only mode preserves native MSA keys, values, idx_keys, and absolute offsets in Block Disk L2 while keeping persistent RAM payloads disabled.
config.m3NativeMsaNote: MiniMax-M3's retained RAM tier is disabled. Enable Block Disk Cache for persistent typed MSA prefix reuse; generic KV q4/q8 remains disabled.
config.openPanguNoPagedNote: openPangu does not use generic paged blocks: causal-convolution state is cumulative and cannot be reconstructed from an arbitrary block. Use Prefix Cache plus prompt-level Disk Cache (L2) instead.
config.pagedKVCacheTooltip: Disabled and locked off for this release. The app always launches --no-paged-cache; Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) is the authoritative reusable-prefix tier.
config.blockSizeTooltipDsv4: DSV4 native SWA+CSA/HCA cache records require fixed 256-token blocks. This value is read-only for this architecture.
config.blockSizeTooltip: Number of tokens per content-addressed SSD cache block. Smaller blocks reduce unused suffix space but increase index and file-management overhead. Default 64 is optimal for most models.
config.maxCacheBlocksTooltip: Maximum number of SSD block-index entries, not a retained RAM allocation. Block 0 is reserved, so indexable token capacity = block_size x (max_blocks - 1). Increase for longer reusable prefixes; disk size is governed separately below.
config.blockDiskPureSsdNote: Block Disk Cache can run as a pure SSD prefix tier while In-Memory Paged Cache remains Off. It keeps only the content-addressed block index in memory, restores KV payloads transiently from SSD, and still requires Prefix Cache.
config.blockDiskCacheTooltip: Persist content-addressed prefix blocks to SSD as the authoritative reusable-prefix tier. Payloads are restored only transiently for reconstruction and preserve each architecture's native full-precision, quantized, compressed, sparse, rotating, or typed state; Auto never adds generic TurboQuant.
config.blockCacheDirectoryTooltip: Managed root for block-level disk cache files. A model/config-specific subdirectory is created automatically, and the size limit applies across all managed subdirectories and typed companions in this root. Leave empty for ~/.cache/vmlx-engine/block-cache/.
config.kvQuantRequiresBatching: KV cache quantization requires continuous batching. Turn on 'Continuous Batching' in the Concurrent Processing section above.
config.kvQuantRequiresPrefix: KV cache quantization requires prefix cache. Enable 'Prefix Cache' above to use KV cache quantization.
config.mixedSwaAutoHint: Mixed sliding/full attention cache detected — Auto preserves the model's native cache-slot and rotating-window metadata and keeps stored prefixes exact, because a quantized stored prefix changes this model's answers when the cache is reused. Generic TurboQuant is not added.
config.storedKvExactRequired: This model interleaves sliding-window and full attention. A quantized stored prefix cache changes its answers when the cache is reused, so only exact storage is offered.
config.hy3AutoHint: HY3 plain-KV cache detected — Auto preserves native KV in live decode and on SSD with no added generic codec. Native MTP D1 copies this cache independently before batch split/verify.
config.bonsaiHybridHint: Bonsai hybrid cache detected — Auto preserves native attention KV and native SSM/GLA companion state without a generic TurboQuant wrapper.
config.qwenHybridHint: Qwen hybrid cache detected — Auto preserves native attention KV and native SSM/GLA companion state without a generic TurboQuant wrapper.
config.qwenFullKvHint: Qwen full-KV cache detected — Auto preserves the model's native full-attention KV representation in live decode and on SSD; no generic TurboQuant codec is added.
config.hybridStatefulHint: Hybrid stateful cache detected — the engine keeps SSM/GLA state native and only uses cache codecs proven for that architecture. Generic TurboQuant KV is disabled unless a tested override exists.
config.dsv4KvQuantHint: DeepSeek-V4 keeps generic TurboQuant KV q4/q8 disabled. Prefix RAM/SSD records preserve native SWA+CSA/HCA state, while CSA/HCA pool quantization is read from the loaded bundle rather than a generic cache-codec override.
config.m3KvQuantHint: MiniMax-M3 keeps generic KV q4/q8 disabled. Prefix reuse uses native MSA snapshots with keys, values, idx_keys, and absolute offsets; generic stored-KV codecs cannot preserve that cache format.
config.openPanguKvQuantHint: openPangu keeps generic KV q4/q8 disabled. Its exact typed snapshot owns MLA KV, DSA indexer, rotating-SWA metadata, and causal-convolution state as one full-precision record.
config.liveCacheCodecTooltip: Auto leaves the CLI flag unset and preserves the exact cache objects created by the loaded architecture: full KV, rotating/sliding, recurrent, sparse, or native compressed/typed composite state. It does not add generic TurboQuant.
config.codecTqOffAll: Live TurboQuant and stored quantization disabled
config.codecHy3: Native HY3 KV (no added cache codec)
config.codecBonsaiHybrid: Native Bonsai attention KV + native hybrid state
config.codecQwenHybrid: Native Qwen attention KV + native hybrid state
config.nativePoolCodecTooltip: This is DSV4's architecture-native compressed-pool codec, not generic TurboQuant KV. The value is detected from the loaded bundle and is not user-overridable from this generic cache panel.
config.dsv4ActivationQatTooltip: Restart required. On enables source-native E4M3 round-trips for attention KV and compressed pools plus Hadamard-128 + FP4 E2M1 indexer round-trips. Off skips only those activation-QAT transforms to avoid their runtime overhead; FP32 compressor staging remains enabled and is not controlled here.
config.dsv4ActivationQatNote: Default Off. Enable only when you want the source-native DSV4 activation-QAT graph and accept its extra runtime work. This switch does not change weights, sampling, cache pool quantization, or FP32 compressor staging.
config.storedCacheQuantTooltip: Controls whether an additional generic codec is imposed at the SSD boundary. Auto preserves the architecture's native representation and adds no codec. Explicit q8/q4 are diagnostic overrides only where supported and may change cache-hit answers; explicit Native/None also adds no codec.
config.groupSizeTooltip: Number of elements quantized together. Smaller groups preserve more precision but use slightly more memory for scale/zero-point metadata. Default 64 is optimal for most models.
config.diskCacheHint: Saves cached prompts to your SSD so they survive server restarts. Next time you load the same model, previous conversations warm up instantly.
config.dsv4LegacyDiskNote: DSV4 uses Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) above for persistent native composite blocks. This legacy whole-prompt disk format remains unavailable for DSV4 typed cache records.
config.legacyDiskNote: Legacy prompt disk cache works with the memory-aware prefix backend. Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) persists content-addressed blocks whether In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM) is On or explicitly Off. Only one disk format can be active at a time.
config.openPanguDiskNote: For openPangu this prompt-level disk cache stores the exact typed N-1 composite and restores it across process restarts. Block Disk Cache remains unavailable.
config.diskCacheRequiresBatching: Disk cache requires continuous batching. Turn on 'Continuous Batching' in the Concurrent Processing section above.
config.legacyDiskPagedConflict: Legacy disk cache is not compatible with In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM). For persistent SSD storage, use 'Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2)' in that section instead. To use legacy Disk Cache, disable the RAM tier first.
config.legacyDiskArchConflict: This architecture requires a native/in-memory paged cache while Prefix Cache is enabled. Use 'Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2)' in the In-Memory Paged Cache section for persistent SSD storage.
config.diskCacheEnablesPrefix: Disk cache is persistent L2 behind Prefix Cache. Turning it on will enable Prefix Cache and disable the in-memory and block-cache backends.
config.enableDiskCacheTooltip: Persist whole-prompt caches to disk for reuse across server restarts. This legacy format acts as L2 behind the memory-aware prefix backend. It requires Prefix Cache and is not compatible with In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM); use Block Disk Cache (SSD / L2) for persistent content-addressed blocks instead.
config.maxCacheSizeTooltip: Maximum disk space for cached prompt states. Oldest entries are evicted when this limit is exceeded. Set to 0 for unlimited. Each cached prompt typically uses 50-500MB depending on model size and prompt length.
config.cacheDirectoryTooltip: Base directory for disk cache files (.safetensors). A model-specific subdirectory is created automatically. Leave empty for the default location (~/.cache/vmlx-engine/prompt-cache/<model>/). Set a custom path if you want to use a specific drive.
config.lightSleepAfterTooltip: Minutes of inactivity before entering light sleep. Light sleep clears KV/prefix caches to free memory but keeps the model loaded in GPU. Wake is instant — no reload needed. Set to 0 to disable light sleep.
config.deepSleepAfterTooltip: Minutes of inactivity before entering deep sleep. Deep sleep unloads the model entirely from GPU memory. The server process stays alive and the model auto-reloads when a new request arrives (2-15 seconds for most models). Set to 0 to disable deep sleep.
config.performanceHint: Controls token streaming, response length, and prompt-window limits. Max Output Tokens caps generated tokens; Max Context Tokens caps accepted prompt/context tokens.
config.modelWideJitTooltip: Compile the entire model forward graph for Metal kernel fusion. This is separate from model-native compiled kernels, which remain automatic when supported. Whole-model JIT requires a trace-safe cache topology and a restart.
config.jitDisabledDsv4: Whole-model JIT is not trace-safe for DeepSeek-V4's path-dependent SWA+CSA/HCA cache. Native compiled decode remains automatic: the supported DSV4 runtime uses compiled router/SwiGLU operations and a fused Metal mHC single-token decode kernel.
config.jitDisabledM3: JIT is disabled for MiniMax-M3 native MSA cache. The Lightning-Indexer idx_keys path must stay on the uncompiled scheduler path.
config.jitDisabledZaya: JIT is disabled for ZAYA typed CCA cache. CCA state is path-dependent and the full cache stack benchmarks faster on the uncompiled scheduler path.
config.jitDisabledMultimodal: JIT is disabled for multimodal/VLM models. The mlx-vlm streaming path owns image/video preprocessing and stream context state that is not safe to trace with mx.compile.
config.jitDisabledHybrid: JIT is disabled for hybrid SSM/Mamba cache models. Their path-dependent Python cache objects are not mx.compile safe.
config.jitDisabledTurboQuant: Server-level mx.compile is disabled for JANGTQ/TurboQuant KV because the live cache uses custom TurboQuant objects that mx.compile cannot trace. JANGTQ fused Metal kernels still run.
config.jitDisabledLaguna: Laguna Auto now preserves native full/sliding cache slots and does not add TurboQuant. Cache Auto therefore does not suppress JIT; any remaining JIT restriction comes from a separate runtime capability gate.
config.jitDisabledFlashMoe: JIT is disabled while Flash MoE is on. Flash MoE's on-demand expert loading is incompatible with mx.compile tracing.
config.jitDisabledDistributed: JIT is disabled while distributed mode is on. Distributed orchestration cannot safely compile the local coordinator graph.
config.dsv4CompiledDecodeHint: Native compiled decode: Automatic. Only unsafe whole-model cache tracing is unavailable.
config.streamIntervalTooltip: Controls how often streaming tokens are sent to the client. A value of 1 sends each token immediately (smoothest streaming). Higher values batch multiple tokens together, which improves throughput but makes streaming feel chunkier. Set to 1 for chat use, higher for batch processing.
config.maxOutputTokensTooltip: Default generated-token cap for this local server. This maps to --max-tokens and only limits response length; it does not change prompt/context length. Leave on Bundle / engine default unless you intentionally want a server-level cap.
config.maxContextTokensTooltip: Maximum prompt/context tokens accepted by this server before prefill. This maps to --max-prompt-tokens and rejects over-limit prompts with prompt_too_long. It does not trim history and does not cap generated output; per-chat/API max_tokens controls output length.
config.generationDefaultsNote: Generation defaults are resolved by the engine from generation_config.json/jang_config when present. The app does not synthesize missing sampling values; per-chat and API request parameters override model defaults.
config.generationDefaultsNoteWithValues: Generation defaults are resolved by the engine from generation_config.json/jang_config when present. Current model-declared values: {values}. The app does not synthesize missing sampling values; per-chat and API request parameters override model defaults.
config.mcpHint: Lets the model call external tools (web search, code execution, etc.) during conversations. Requires a model that supports tool calling.
config.mcpConfigFileTooltip: Path to a JSON config file defining MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool servers. When configured, the model can call external tools during generation. The config file defines tool server endpoints, authentication, and available capabilities.
config.enabledMcpServersTooltip: Comma or newline separated server names from mcp.json. Empty means every configured server is eligible for this session.
config.disabledMcpServersTooltip: Comma or newline separated server names to block even when they are present in mcp.json.
config.enabledMcpToolsTooltip: Comma or newline separated MCP tool names, usually server__tool. Empty means every server-eligible tool is eligible unless denied below.
config.disabledMcpToolsTooltip: Comma or newline separated MCP tool names to block even if the model asks for them.
config.automaticToolChoiceTooltip: Auto follows the detected model/tool-parser contract. On explicitly enables automatic tool selection. Off explicitly disables it.
config.autoDetectCurrently: Auto-detect is currently {value} for this model.
config.toolCallParserTooltip: Specifies how to parse the model's tool call output. Each model family uses a different format (Qwen, Llama, Mistral, Hermes, DeepSeek, GLM, etc). 'Auto-detect' reads config.json to pick the right one. If auto-detection fails (e.g. GGUF, renamed fine-tunes), select the parser matching your model's base architecture. Click '?' to see format examples and supported models for each parser.
config.reasoningParserTooltip: Separates reasoning/thinking from final content. Use Auto-detect unless it picks wrong. Qwen3: Qwen, QwQ, MiniMax, StepFun (strict <think> tags). DeepSeek R1: DeepSeek-R1, GLM-4.7, Phi-4, Nemotron (lenient <think> tags). GPT-OSS: GLM-4.7 Flash (Harmony protocol). Mistral 4: Mistral Small/Large 4 ([THINK] tags). Click '?' for full model list.
config.parserFinetunesNote: Fine-tunes inherit the base model's parser. A Llama fine-tune uses llama, a Qwen fine-tune uses qwen, regardless of its marketing name. When auto-detect fails, select the parser matching the base architecture.
config.modelFamilyOverrideTooltip: Force the model family instead of letting the engine autodetect it from jang_config.json / config.json. Use this for renamed fine-tunes, GGUF, or custom merges where detection picks the wrong family. The chosen family's cache + tool/reasoning parser contract is applied. Leave on Auto unless detection is wrong — forcing a family whose cache contract mismatches the weights (e.g. forcing a plain-KV family onto a hybrid/SSM or MLA model) can produce garbled output.
config.customChatTemplateTooltip: Override the model's built-in Jinja2 chat template. Useful when the default template is incompatible with your client (e.g., JetBrains AI Chat). Leave empty to use the model's built-in template. The template receives 'messages' and 'add_generation_prompt' variables.
config.multimodalSupportTooltip: Vision-Language Model mode for models like Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Pixtral, InternVL, or LLaVA. Auto uses the detected model/runtime policy. Force Off remains an explicit user override. Smelt and documented unsafe runtimes use text-only loading.
config.dsv4TextRuntimeNote: DSV4 Flash is served through the text runtime. Image/video controls stay hidden because this bundle has no VL processor path.
config.vlmDisabledSmelt: VLM is disabled when Smelt Mode is active. Smelt uses text-only loading for partial expert support.
config.forceTextOnlyNote: This bundle includes media metadata, but its detected vMLX runtime is currently text-only. Attachments stay disabled until that family's native media path is live-verified; changing quantization format alone does not make the media route available.
config.vlmActiveNote: VLM mode is active — the MLLM scheduler handles image/video processing with Prefix Cache, In-Memory Paged Cache (RAM), and KV quantization support.
config.vlmOffNote: VLM mode is off only when the model is not auto-detected as multimodal. Detected VLM bundles launch with image/video support.
config.omniBackendTooltip: Nemotron-Omni encoder backend. Stage 1 is the correctness-first PyTorch/MPS bridge. Stage 2 maps to --omni-backend stage2 / VMLX_OMNI_BACKEND=stage2 for native MLX RADIO + Parakeet benchmarking.
config.imageTokenBudgetTooltip: Gemma 4 visual soft-token budget per image. 280 is the bundle default; use 560 or 1120 for OCR and small text at higher prefill cost. The selected value is sent as image_token_budget and is part of the media cache identity.
config.videoFpsTooltip: For VL models with video support (Qwen 3.6, Qwen3.5-VL). Controls how many frames per second are sampled from an uploaded video clip. Lower = fewer frames = faster prefill but less temporal detail. Qwen 3.6's temporal embeddings tolerate up to ~4 fps; 2 fps is a good default.
config.maxVideoFramesTooltip: Maximum number of frames extracted from a single video, regardless of fps or duration. Caps prefill cost on long clips. Qwen 3.6 supports up to 32+ frames but most prompts work well with 8.
config.nativeMtpBlockedFallback: Native MTP weights were detected, but this bundle has not passed the runtime compatibility gate. Autoregressive decode remains active.
config.nativeMtpHint: Uses the model's preserved MTP heads when supported. Fixed depth sets the requested ceiling; adaptive selects depth at runtime. Models without compatible MTP heads use ordinary autoregressive decode.
config.nativeMtpAutoNote: Auto uses greedy startup defaults (temperature 0). Explicit API/chat sampling overrides these defaults; compatible sampled requests use rejection-sampling MTP. Unsupported sampling combinations use ordinary autoregressive decode, with the reason reported in Performance.
config.nativeMtpDefaultOffNote: Auto uses ordinary autoregressive decode for this model because its current MTP verifier has not beaten AR. Choose a fixed D1-D3 depth to opt into MTP explicitly.
config.nativeMtpDeterministicNote: Explicit deterministic mode enforces greedy sampling for every API/chat request. Depth is controlled separately below. Choose Off if per-request sampled values must remain authoritative.
config.nativeMtpModeTooltip: Auto uses greedy startup defaults but honors explicit request sampling. Deterministic enforces greedy sampling for every request. Off disables the in-model MTP runtime.
config.nativeMtpDepthTooltip: Maximum tokens drafted per native-MTP verification cycle. Adaptive uses an exact sampling-profile measurement when available; Fixed uses the selected D1-D3 ceiling.
config.nativeMtpDepthPolicyTooltip: Adaptive may promote or demote an exact-profile starting depth from live acceptance and cost; an unmeasured sampled profile stays on AR. Fixed disables request-level depth adaptation and uses D1, D2, or D3 as the selected ceiling. At D3, a low-confidence first proposal may stop the remaining draft chain to avoid a measured slowdown.
config.nativeMtpDepthAdaptiveNote: Adaptive uses a measured profile matching the request's sampling mode. An unmeasured sampled profile remains on ordinary AR until current-runtime evidence can enable MTP safely.
config.nativeMtpDepthFixedNote: Fixed uses D{depth} as the request ceiling. D1-D2 draft that depth; at D3, a low-confidence first proposal may stop the remaining draft chain instead of paying for predictions unlikely to be accepted.
config.nativeMtpDetectedNote: Detected scope: {scope}; native cache: {cache}; depth source: {depthSource}. Hybrid cache bundles keep KV blocks and typed SSM companion state in the SSD cache contract; retained paged RAM stays disabled.
config.specDecodeHint: Use a small draft model to propose tokens, then verify them in a single target model pass. Can give 20-90% speedup with zero quality loss.
config.specDecodeIncompatBatching: Speculative decoding is incompatible with continuous batching. The draft model is omitted at launch while the cache-stack scheduler is active.
config.specDecodeIncompatVlm: VLM speculative decoding requires a matched DFlash2 draft. Other draft models are omitted at launch for VLM requests.
config.draftModelTooltip: Path or HuggingFace name of a small draft model. Must use the same tokenizer as the main model. Example: mlx-community/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-4bit for a Llama 3 target model. Leave empty to disable speculative decoding.
config.draftTokensPerStepTooltip: Number of tokens the draft model proposes per speculative decoding step. Higher values = more potential speedup but lower acceptance rate. Sweet spot is typically 2-5.
config.preAlphaWarnBody1: This feature is under active development and is not safe to expose on any network you don't fully control.
config.preAlphaWarnBody2: Known gaps: cluster secret is sent plaintext over the wire (no TLS, no HMAC); worker crash recovery is not implemented; coordinator-loss re-election recovery is a stub; protocol has no version handshake; tensor parallelism is stubbed.
config.preAlphaUsage: Recommended usage today: run one vmlx-worker on the same Mac you're running the coordinator on (different port), bound to 127.0.0.1, as a smoke test. Real multi-Mac deployment is blocked behind Phase 2 hardening. See docs/guides/distributed-setup.md.
config.distributedHint: Pipeline parallelism splits transformer layers across nodes. Each request passes hidden states over a TCP connection between workers. In localhost loopback testing, the overhead is dominated by the loopback memcpy — useful for verifying correctness, not performance.
config.enableDistributedTooltip: Split the model across multiple Macs. Requires vmlx-worker running on each additional Mac. The coordinator (this Mac) handles tokenization, embedding, and final projection.
config.distributedDisabledFlashMoe: Distributed is disabled while Flash MoE is on. Flash MoE patches local model layers — distributed workers have their own model copies.
config.parallelismModeTooltip: Pipeline: split layers across nodes (simple, works with any network). Tensor: split weights within layers (requires high bandwidth, 10GbE+ recommended).
config.tensorNotImplemented: Tensor parallelism is not yet implemented. Use pipeline parallelism for now.
config.clusterSecretTooltip: Shared secret for authenticating worker nodes. All workers must use the same secret. Leave empty for no authentication (only safe on trusted networks).
config.workerNodesNote: Worker nodes: Install vMLX on each Mac and run 'vmlx-worker --secret YOUR_SECRET' from Terminal. Workers auto-advertise via Bonjour — the coordinator discovers them automatically.
config.setupStep3: 3. Workers appear automatically above via Bonjour discovery
config.setupStep4: 4. Or click "Add Manual" to add by IP if discovery doesn't find them
config.setupNetworkNote: Thunderbolt 5: ~120 Gbps, 0.1ms latency (best). 1GbE: works fine for pipeline parallelism. WiFi: works but slower. Any network that can ping the other Mac will work.
config.embeddingModelTooltip: Pre-load a separate embedding model at startup for the /v1/embeddings endpoint. Runs alongside the main chat model. Example: mlx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-6bit. Leave empty to disable embeddings endpoint.
config.additionalArgsTooltip: Raw command-line arguments appended to the serve command. Use this for flags not exposed in the UI above. Example: --log-level DEBUG. Arguments are split by whitespace and passed directly to the CLI.
config.metalWiredLimitHelp: If a large model hits Metal OOM, SIGKILL, or kernel-panic risk, macOS may need a tuned Metal wired-memory limit. Example for large-memory Macs: {{command}}. Do not set it equal to physical RAM; leave OS/WindowServer/app headroom. On 128GB Macs, 115000-120000 MB is usually safer than 128000 MB. The command requires an admin password and resets after reboot.
config.pagedCacheCapacity: Effective in-memory cache capacity: {{blockSize}} tokens/block x {{usableBlocks}} usable blocks ({{maxBlocks}} configured; 1 reserved) = {{tokens}} tokens
config.pagedCacheMemoryIgnored: Cache TTL does not apply while In-Memory Paged Cache is on. Cache Memory Limit / Cache Memory % caps its L1 use of Apple unified memory; Max Cache Blocks and Block Size cap token capacity.
config.blockDiskCapacity: Effective SSD block-index capacity: {{blockSize}} tokens/block x {{usableBlocks}} usable blocks ({{maxBlocks}} configured; 1 reserved) = {{tokens}} tokens
config.ramCacheTradeoffNotice: SSD-only cache policy: In-Memory Paged Cache and Media Preprocess RAM Cache are locked OFF for every model. Reusable prompts persist on SSD and cache payloads are restored only transiently; image, video, and audio processor tensors are released after every request.
config.blockCacheSavedGbOverride: Saved explicit limit: {gb} GB. This overrides the percentage above until you change it. Changing the percentage replaces this saved GB limit.
config.blockCacheMaxPercentTooltip: Maximum physical disk space for the managed block-cache root, as a percent of this volume. Sizing by percent keeps the cache proportionate to the machine instead of a fixed number of gigabytes. The budget is shared across model/config namespaces and typed companion state: the size limit applies across all managed subdirectories and typed companions in this root, and when several live sessions each supply a percentage the smallest finite limit is enforced. Set to 0 for unlimited only when no live session supplies a finite limit.
config.blockCacheSharedBudgetNote: This budget is shared by all sessions — the app keeps one cache folder and removes the oldest prompts across every model when it fills up, including models you are not using right now.
config.clearSsdCache: Clear SSD cache for this session
config.clearSsdCacheTooltip: Deletes this session's cached prompts from the SSD. The next message will be a fresh prompt with no cache to reuse. The session must be running.
config.clearSsdCacheFailed: Could not clear: {{error}}. The session must be running.
config.clearSsdCacheEmpty: Nothing to clear — this session had no cached prompts.
config.clearSsdCachePartial: Cleared {{count}} tier(s); {{skipped}} was left alone (still in use by a running request). Try again once the session is idle.
config.blockCacheArchitecturePoolNote: One pool for everything: this budget covers every cache type vMLX writes — plain KV blocks, typed companion state (SSM/GatedDelta), native composite records (DeepSeek-V4 DSA/CSA/HCA), rotating sliding-window state, and multimodal blocks — for every model and every session. When it fills, the oldest prompts are removed first, across all of them, including models you are not using right now.
config.videoMaxPixelsTooltip: Maximum pixels per sampled video frame after resizing (aspect ratio preserved, rounded to the model's patch size). Lower = fewer vision tokens per frame = faster prefill, less spatial detail. Leave at Processor default to keep the model's own sizing. The native loader caps this at 602k.
config.videoTokenBudgetTooltip: Approximate cap on vision tokens for each video attachment (images are not included; it never limits output tokens or context). The engine turns it into a per-clip pixel budget (tokens × the model's pixels per video token; 2,048 for Qwen3-VL) that the video loader spreads across the sampled frames; frames still round to the model's patch size and the processor keeps its own whole-clip bounds, so the exact count can differ. The engine log line 'Video processed' shows the real token count.

cachePanel.reuseExplainer: Reuse matches the longest continuous causal token prefix from token 0. Only the unmatched tail is prefilled; arbitrary suffix or interior sequences are never reused. On path-dependent families (DeepSeek V4, ZAYA CCA, and rotating-KV models such as Gemma 4 and Muse) a prompt SHORTER than the cached chain may reuse nothing and prefill in full.

prompt.maskTitle: Paint a mask to select which areas to fill/replace
prompt.stepsTip: Number of denoising steps. More steps = higher quality but slower. Schnell/Z-Image: 4 steps. Dev: 20 steps. Qwen Edit: 28 steps.
prompt.sizeTip: Output image dimensions. Must be multiples of 16. Larger = more VRAM and slower. 1024x1024 is standard.
prompt.guidanceTip: Classifier-free guidance scale. Higher = more prompt adherence but less creative freedom. 3-5 for Flux models, 7-12 for other models.
prompt.strengthEditTip: How much to change the source image. 0 = no change, 1 = completely new. For edits, 0.6-0.8 works well.
prompt.sourcePreservationTip: Native mflux source preservation: higher values keep more of the source and run fewer denoising steps; lower values allow larger changes. With few steps, a high value may leave little or no denoising. The value sent to the API is unchanged.
prompt.strengthVariationTip: Adapter-specific variation strength. Its direction and effective step count depend on the loaded model.
prompt.placeholderVariation: Add to prompt for next variation (or leave empty for random variation)...
prompt.placeholderNeedSource: Upload a source image above, then describe your edit...
prompt.placeholderNeedMask: Paint a mask first (click "Paint Mask" above), then describe what to fill...
prompt.placeholderEdit: Describe the edit to apply (e.g., "make the sky purple")...
prompt.placeholderGenerate: Describe the image you want to generate...

settings.stepsTitle: Number of denoising iterations. More steps = better quality but slower. Schnell works well at 4, Dev needs 20+.
settings.sizeTitle: Output image dimensions. Larger = more detail but slower and more memory. 1024x1024 is standard.
settings.guidanceTitle: How closely the image follows your prompt. Higher = more literal, lower = more creative. Default 3.5 works for most prompts.
settings.seedTitle: Random seed for reproducibility. Same seed + same prompt = same image. Leave empty for random.
settings.strengthTitle: How much to change the source image. 0.0 = no change, 1.0 = completely redrawn. 0.7-0.85 works well for most edits.
settings.countTitle: How many images to generate per prompt. Each uses the same settings but different random seeds. Max 4.
settings.quantizeTitle: Model precision. Set when starting the server and cannot be changed while running.
settings.negativePlaceholder: Things to avoid in the image...
settings.serverManagedAutomatically: Server settings are managed automatically for image models.
settings.negativeHelpBody: Describe what you don't want in the image. Useful for avoiding common artifacts. Example:
settings.negativeHelpExample: "blurry, low quality, text, watermark, deformed hands"
settings.strengthNotUsed: Strength is not used by {model}: this edit model conditions on the source image.
settings.negativeNotUsed: Negative prompt is not used by {model}.
